entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Novella d'Andrea (1312–1366) was an Italian legal scholar and professor in law at the University of Bologna.

Born in Bologna, Italy, she studied at the University of Bologna, where she became a renowned expert in Roman law.

Her most notable contribution was the development of the 'Novellae d'Andrea,' a comprehensive legal code that integrated Roman law with Italian custom.

This code had a lasting impact on the development of Italian law, influencing subsequent generations of legal scholars.

The code's significance extends beyond Italy, as it reflects the cultural exchange and legal evolution that occurred during the medieval period.

As a female academic in a male-dominated field, Novella d'Andrea's achievements are all the more remarkable.

In her own time, she was recognized for her expertise, and her work has been rediscovered and studied by modern scholars.

Today, her legacy serves as a testament to the power of women in shaping the course of legal history.
